grain.chemistry: Organic carbohydrate/protein material. Absorbs moisture, susceptible to mould, infestation, and odour transfer. Regulated under International Grain Code (not IMSBC) but broker-treated as Class C equivalent for compatibility.
grain.broker_notes: Grain clean required before loading. Holds must be dry, odour-free, insect-free, no trace of previous cargo residues. Prior coal or petcoke cargo = must wash + deodorise + re-inspect. Prior fertilizer = almost certainly fail inspection.

steel.chemistry: Ferrous metal product (iron + carbon alloy). Does not contaminate other cargoes chemically, but surface rust (iron oxide) and mill scale can stain hold surfaces and subsequent cargoes.
steel.broker_notes: Hospital clean required before loading steel coils — even small rust stains can cause cargo damage claims. Hold paintwork must be intact. Prior bulk cargo (coal, ore) requires thorough washing before steel loading.

pipes.chemistry: Steel or iron alloy (line pipe, casing, drill pipe). Similar to steel but often protective coatings (epoxy, FBE) present. Project cargo, typically stowed/lashed.
pipes.broker_notes: Hospital clean required. Pipes have threaded ends or protective caps — contamination or damage to connections is a major claim driver. Prior dirty bulk (coal, ore) absolutely requires full wash and inspection.

iron-ore.imsbc_section: IRON ORE FINES / IRON ORE PELLETS
iron-ore.chemistry: Iron oxides (Fe2O3, Fe3O4). Fines are fine-particled and moisture-sensitive — liable to liquefy above TML. Pellets and lumps are Group C (no liquefaction). Dense cargo, high stowage factor risk.
contamination_risk: red dust contamination of subsequent food cargoes
iron-ore.broker_notes: Normal clean acceptable for next iron ore or coal cargo. Before grain or food cargo: thorough wash + dry required. Iron ore fines require TML certificate from shipper — if moisture > TML, loading must be refused.

dri.chemistry: Metallic iron (>90% Fe) in sponge/briquette/fines form. Highly porous, reacts with oxygen (self-heating to >900°C) and water (generates H2 gas). Must be shipped under inert atmosphere (N2). HBI is least reactive, DRI fines most reactive.
contamination_risk: inert gas atmosphere interference with other cargo monitoring
dri.broker_notes: Extremely dangerous cargo — dedicated voyages preferred. Never stow adjacent to water-carrying cargo or coal. Inert gas blanketing required throughout voyage. After DRI, thorough inspection of hold for residual metallic dust before any cargo.

coal.chemistry: Carbonaceous sedimentary rock. Sub-bituminous and bituminous coals emit methane (CH4) and CO; liable to spontaneous combustion. Fine-grained coals may also have Group A (liquefaction) characteristics requiring TML certificate.
coal.broker_notes: After coal: heavy alkaline degreaser wash, multiple applications needed for stubborn stains. Before grain: usually requires full wash + inspection + surveyor sign-off. Methane emission cargoes require continuous ventilation — opposite of self-heating protocol.

petcoke.chemistry: Carbon-rich residue from petroleum refining. Uncalcined (green) petcoke is oily, high sulphur, liable to spontaneous heating above 55°C. Calcined petcoke is harder, shinier, still high dust. Both produce black oily persistent staining.
contamination_risk: vanadium/nickel trace metals in uncalcined grades
petcoke.broker_notes: Most demanding cleaning after discharge — oily petcoke requires alkaline degreaser + deodoriser, multiple wash cycles. Green petcoke above 55°C cannot be loaded. After petcoke, assume 2–3 extra cleaning days before grain-clean standard.

fertilizer.imsbc_section: AMMONIUM NITRATE BASED FERTILIZER MHB / FERTILIZER (various schedules)
fertilizer.chemistry: Highly variable: urea (inert, hygroscopic), DAP/MAP (acidic dust), potash/MOP (corrosive), ammonium nitrate (oxidiser, self-sustaining decomposition risk). Mixed fertilisers may fall Group B (MHB OH) or Group C depending on AN content. All are hygroscopic.
fertilizer.broker_notes: Hospital clean required before fertilizer loading. After fertilizer: thorough acid/alkaline wash required — traces cause grain contamination (as little as 0.001% sugar-equivalent in cement destroys it; similar risk with fertilizer residue in grain). AN-based fertilizers require segregation from oxidiser-incompatible goods.

cement.chemistry: Calcium silicate/aluminate powder. Clinker loaded hot (>100°C possible) damages hold paintwork. Reacts with water to form hard calcium hydroxide deposits. Corrosive to eyes/skin; alkaline dust. Seawater contamination raises chloride content (damages construction quality).
contamination_risk: calcium deposits fuse to hold surfaces
chloride contamination from seawater during washing
cement.broker_notes: After cement: immediate dry sweep then hydrochloric acid descale required — delayed cleaning allows cement to cure permanently onto steel. Before next cargo, full acid wash + inspection. Grain clean minimum required for most commodities after cement.

sulphur.chemistry: Elemental sulphur. Dry sulphur inert to bare steel; wet sulphur highly corrosive (forms H2SO4). Dust forms explosive mixtures with air. IMSBC: Group B (MHB); UN 1350 = Class 4.1 flammable solid. Corrosive to hold steelwork via sulphuric acid formation.
sulphur.broker_notes: After sulphur: fresh water wash (NOT seawater — avoids acid formation), thorough dry before inspection. Grain clean standard barely achievable after sulphur without multiple washes. Holds must be well protected — wet sulphur is highly corrosive. Never sweep dry sulphur dust (explosion risk).

scrap.imsbc_section: FERROUS METAL BORINGS, SHAVINGS, TURNINGS or CUTTINGS UN 2793 / SCRAP METAL
scrap.chemistry: Mixed ferrous and non-ferrous metal fragments. Contamination with oily rags, cutting fluids, lubricants, plastics, tyres, batteries creates fire/explosion risk. Shavings/turnings: oxidise rapidly, self-heat. HMS and shredded scrap: lower self-heat risk but high impurity risk.
scrap.broker_notes: Scrap quality varies enormously — surveyor inspection before loading mandatory. Shredded scrap with cutting oil: self-heating risk, keep dry. After scrap: oil degreasing required before food-grade cargo. Impurity inspection (batteries, oil filters) is shipper obligation under IMSBC.

bauxite.chemistry: Aluminium oxide-hydroxide ore (gibbsite, boehmite, diaspore). Fine-grained bauxite susceptible to liquefaction (Group A). Coarse bauxite may be Group C. Red/brown dust from iron oxide content. Abrasive. Low chemical reactivity.
bauxite.broker_notes: TML certificate mandatory for bauxite fines — BULK JUPITER casualty (2015) killed 18 crew due to liquefaction. Normal clean for next ore/coal. Before grain: full wash + surveyor inspection required. Red dust staining difficult to remove.

general.chemistry: Broker/operational term for mixed or miscellaneous cargo — no specific IMSBC schedule. May cover project cargo, bagged goods, palletised commodities, or multi-commodity shipments. Chemistry varies by actual cargo.
general.broker_notes: Not a regulatory category — used by freight brokers to group unclassified or mixed cargoes. Compatibility must be assessed case-by-case based on actual cargo. L5C matrix should treat 'general' as requiring manual surveyor review for each specific pair.

sugar.chemistry: Sucrose (C12H22O11). Hygroscopic, absorbs moisture forming caked residue. Contaminates cement/concrete drastically (even 0.001% traces destroy cement setting). Requires grain-clean equivalent holds. Susceptible to odour transfer.
sugar.broker_notes: Grain clean required before sugar. After sugar: wash with warm water — sweet residue attracts insects and promotes mould. Prior fertilizer or chemical cargo = almost certain rejection by sugar surveyor. Sugar is highly reactive with alkaline residues (cement, lime).

salt.chemistry: Sodium chloride (NaCl). Highly corrosive to bare steel (pitting, hold damage). Does not contaminate most industrial cargoes chemically, but chloride residue is problematic for construction materials (cement, rebar). Food-grade sea salt requires clean holds.
salt.broker_notes: Normal clean after salt — but thorough fresh water rinse essential to remove chloride residue before any metal cargo (accelerates corrosion) or food cargo. Prior coal/petcoke requires full clean before salt for food-grade. Salt severely corrodes unprotected hold steelwork.

limestone.chemistry: Calcium carbonate (CaCO3) or calcium-magnesium carbonate. Alkaline dust. Chemically inert in ambient conditions. Abrasive dust. Low contamination risk for most cargoes. Dolomite similar profile.
contamination_risk: white dust staining of subsequent sensitive cargo
limestone.broker_notes: One of the 'cleanest' bulk cargoes — normal clean acceptable for most subsequent cargoes. Alkaline nature means slight incompatibility with acid-sensitive cargoes. Before grain, standard wash and inspection. Very low contamination profile makes it a good 'buffer' voyage.

manganese ore.chemistry: Manganese oxides (MnO2, Mn2O3). Fines: Group A (liquefaction above TML). Coarse: Group C. Dense cargo (low stowage factor — risk of tank top overstress). Dust irritating to eyes and mucous membranes. Reacts with acids/alkalis/oxidisers to produce toxic MnO vapour.
manganese ore.broker_notes: TML certificate mandatory for fines. Dust is health hazard — crew must wear respirators. Dense cargo: structural loading plan mandatory (tank top stress). After manganese: thorough wash before food or clean cargo. Dark staining persistent and hard to remove.

copper concentrate.chemistry: Copper sulphides (chalcopyrite CuFeS2, chalcocite Cu2S) typically 20–35% Cu. Group A (liquefaction). Also Group B hazards (MHB SH, TX, CR): reacts with water to generate H2S (toxic), contains arsenic/lead/zinc trace impurities. Oily acidic slurry appearance when wet.
contamination_risk: H2S gas release toxic to crew
copper concentrate.broker_notes: Dual-hazard cargo (Group A + B properties). TML and moisture content certificates mandatory. Dedicated voyage strongly preferred — extreme contamination risk for virtually any other cargo. After copper concentrate: full acid wash + inspection before any other cargo. Manual surveyor review required for any adjacent cargo.
